name: Michael Novogratz

career.title: Money market salesman, then sales and trading roles in Tokyo and Hong Kong; partner from 1998
Principal; co-chief investment officer of macro funds and director

background_rationale: Founded Galaxy Digital in 2018 after a long career as a macro trader and partner at Goldman Sachs and Fortress Investment Group.

notable.summary: Galaxy completed a corporate reorganization and its Class A common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker GLXY.
Galaxy closed a $1.4 billion project financing to convert its Helios campus in West Texas into an AI and high-performance computing data center leased to CoreWeave.
Galaxy completed its voluntary delisting from the Toronto Stock Exchange, leaving Nasdaq as its sole listing.

In his 2025 annual letter, Novogratz wrote that Galaxy had spent eight years building around the conviction that digital assets and blockchain will reshape global finance, and described the Nasdaq listing as a beginning rather than a destination.

personal_story.hook: A Princeton wrestling captain and former military helicopter pilot, he rebuilt his career on crypto after leaving Fortress.
personal_story.summary: Novogratz was raised in Alexandria, Virginia, the third of seven children of a West Point football lineman. He was a Virginia high school wrestling runner-up and went on to captain Princeton's wrestling team while earning an economics degree. After serving as a military helicopter pilot, he joined Goldman Sachs in 1989 as a money market salesman, spent most of the 1990s in Tokyo and Hong Kong, and made partner in 1998. He later became a principal at Fortress Investment Group, where his macro funds suffered heavy losses before he retired in 2015. His crypto journey began in 2013, and in 2018 he launched Galaxy to bring institutions into blockchain.
